paragraphs: Apkolos. Tosefta, Chullin, chapter 8: poultry is neither placed nor eaten [with cheese]; Yehudah calls it a Beit Shammai leniency, etc. Elazar son of Tzadok allows placing it with cheese; Apkolos forbids eating. Others report in his name that it may even be eaten. When does the table restriction apply? On a dining table. On a table that is not used for eating, one may put a piece of meat on one side and cheese on the other. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permits even a dining table. End quotation. Chullin 104b: Agra, Rabbi Abba’s father-in-law, teaches that poultry and cheese may be eaten, etc., be-apkolos in Heilprin’s quotation. Ran explains the Rif’s be-apkolis as “with a cloth.” The checked Bavli reads be-apikoran. Tosefta instead makes Apkolos a sage’s name.
